clue.text: Rejected batsman bags century against India — what do selectors do?

indicators.note: to bag something is to take it in, so the batsman's letters enclose the others
something rejected is sent back, so the batsman's initials are read from the end

parts.note: KP is Kevin Pietersen, the England batsman known by his initials

indicators.note: against here means up beside, so the two letters are placed side by side

parts.note: I is India in the radio alphabet
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A dropped England batsman takes his place again for a hundred against India, leaving fans wondering how the selectors choose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns KP round to PK, and 'bags' puts IC inside it: I and C sit together, 'against' meaning next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Selectors choose a team, so what they do is select players for it.

clue.text: Hail Queen leaving Frozen performance?

indicators.note: the Queen is leaving, so her letters are taken out of the hail

parts.note: hail is a shower of ice falling from the sky
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A greeting to the Queen as she walks out of the Disney film Frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' reads as a greeting to the Queen, but it is a downpour of ice pellets; 'Frozen' looks like the film title.
explanation.definitionFit: A skating spectacle is staged on ice, a frozen surface, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Extremely nice family stories in case of doubt

parts.note: kin means one's family or relatives

indicators.note: in places the stories inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside, so only the first and last letters of doubt are used

parts.note: lies are untrue stories

explanation.surface: Someone thoughtful tells family tales whenever there is uncertainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of doubt' gives D and T, the outer letters, with LIES put between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindliest is the superlative of kindly, so it means nicest to the utmost degree.

clue.text: Made mistake getting revolutionary drug — I can't take any more

indicators.note: made in the sense of reworked or fashioned into something new, so these letters get rearranged
revolutionary means turning round, so the drug is read backwards

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, a drug

explanation.surface: Someone who has blundered by taking a radical drug cries that they have had enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' rearranges MISTAKE as MAKEITS; 'revolutionary' turns POT into TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are the plea of someone overwhelmed who wants an ordeal ended.

clue.text: Stuck up ladder impatience shows

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from the bottom
shows means the letters are on display within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone up a ladder reveals their impatience while being stuck there.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'shows' as the definition, but 'Stuck' is the definition, 'up' the reversal and 'shows' the hidden signal; DERIM read upwards is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stuck in a difficulty, as if in a bog, is a fixed sense of this word.

clue.text: Union activity's going to spell termination of employment

parts.note: knocking off is British slang for having sex, a union of two people
a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: A trade union's industrial action threatens to put staff out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union activity' looks like a strike, but it is sexual union. The definition reads like dismissal but means the end of the working day.
explanation.definitionFit: The time when work stops for the day is when employment ends for that shift, a playful reading.

clue.text: Seen Colin's bruised lip?

indicators.note: bruised means battered out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone has noticed Colin's swollen, injured mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lip' looks like part of Colin's face, but it is cheeky backchat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip is slang for cheeky, disrespectful talk, which is impudence.

clue.text: False hope at the end — that's sad

parts.note: a sham is something false or fake

indicators.note: at the end picks out the final letter of hope

explanation.surface: Hope that proves false in the end is a sad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation what a pity, expressing regret, is how the word is used here.

clue.text: Isn't backing attitudes at work

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work, especially of music
attitudes are postures or poses

explanation.surface: Someone does not support the way people behave in the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but the definition means resisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is against a plan resists it rather than supporting it.

clue.text: Sign on — one way to feed artist

indicators.note: to feed is to put into, so these letters go inside the sign

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
A means one, a single thing
RD, short for road, is a way

explanation.surface: A painter signs on to a scheme as a way of earning his keep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to feed' puts ON, A and RD inside LEO, between its E and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Italian Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa, an artist by example.

clue.text: Grant the politician has misused with assistant initially

indicators.note: misused means put to wrong use, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: PPS, a Parliamentary Private Secretary, is an MP's assistant known by initials

explanation.surface: A grant that a politician and his helper have misspent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like money; it is the first name of the Conservative minister Grant Shapps.
explanation.definitionFit: Grant Shapps is a British Conservative MP and cabinet minister.

clue.text: Really like endless deaths, bar one perhaps, in film

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement of the letters, so they are reordered
endless means the final letter of like is dropped

parts.note: A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A film where nearly everyone dies, except possibly one character.
explanation.walkthrough: REALLY, LIK and DEATHS pooled, with 'bar one' taking out an A, and the rest rearranged ('perhaps'). The 1955 Ealing comedy fits: all the gang die, the old lady survives.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1955 Ealing comedy about a gang of robbers, remade in 2004.

clue.text: Country clothes precious to police officer out of uniform

parts.note: precious in the sense of affectedly dainty means twee
a DS, detective sergeant, is a plain-clothes officer

explanation.surface: Rural garments are a bit too dainty for a plain-clothes copper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed suits and jackets are traditional wear for the British countryside.

clue.text: Prickly type upsetting China? Sure

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is a touchy person annoying China? Certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prickly type' suggests a grumpy person; it is a spiny sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: This marine creature is covered in sharp spines, so it is literally prickly.

clue.text: Pants, new ones, worn at various points

indicators.note: worn means worn out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: N, S and E are several compass points

explanation.surface: New underpants put on at different times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like underwear, but it is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang pants means rubbish or drivel, as in that's pants.

clue.text: Listened secretly as barrister mentioned this place in Bow earlier

indicators.note: earlier puts the sounded word before the barrister's letters
mentioned means spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: Bow is in the East End of London, where the Cockney here drops its H
a barrister in court wears a wig, so is wigged

explanation.surface: A barrister claims he eavesdropped while mentioning a place in Bow some time ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a Cockney district of London; the Cockney says 'ere for here, which sounds like ear.
explanation.definitionFit: To earwig is British slang for eavesdropping on a conversation.

clue.text: He won't reproduce form at start of Royal Ascot

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so these letters are shaped into a new order
start of picks out the opening letter of Royal

explanation.surface: A racehorse's form at the opening of Royal Ascot means it will not be put to stud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like racing form; it is the anagram signal. Royal Ascot is a famous race meeting in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer castrated before puberty to keep a high voice cannot father children.

clue.text: Joined Times — want to frame following article

indicators.note: following places these letters after the article

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: to frame means to surround, so want encloses the times sign

parts.note: to want is to need
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Someone joined The Times newspaper, eager to write the next article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Annexed means attached or joined on, as a territory added to a state.

clue.text: Politician having frisky encounter with unmarried bird

indicators.note: unmarried takes away M, the abbreviation for married

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
a romp is a playful sexual encounter

explanation.surface: A politician caught in a sexual fling with a single young woman, a tabloid story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is British slang for a young woman in the surface, but here it is the emu.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the European Parliament is an elected politician.

clue.text: Fury — big-time

parts.note: mega means very big
an era is a period of time

explanation.definitionFit: Megaera was one of the three Furies, avenging spirits of Greek myth.

clue.text: Conciliatory words after spasm of anger's held in

indicators.note: a spasm is a convulsion, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Peace-making words after a fit of temper has been kept under control.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to show that no resentment remains after a quarrel, smoothing things over.

clue.text: Hurry — male in women's quarters!

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, to hurry

explanation.surface: A warning to rush, as a man has strayed into the women's rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: In a Muslim household the harem is the separate part where the women live.

clue.text: Supply nurse's expected

parts.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse in Britain
due means expected, as in a train being due

explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or provide someone with a quality.

clue.text: Old Henry accommodates a Catholic bishop

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so these letters go inside

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in an ex-wife
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
RC is short for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: An elderly Henry gives a Catholic bishop somewhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Henry' looks like a king, but it is EX and H.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Eastern churches an exarch is a senior bishop ranking above a metropolitan.

clue.text: Plants turn into papers (ours)

indicators.note: into places the turn inside the papers

parts.note: this puzzle appears in the Independent, so its papers are the Indies
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Flowers made into newspapers, ours among them.
explanation.walkthrough: '(ours)' tells the solver the papers are those of the Independent, which ran this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo plants of the pea family yield a blue dye.

clue.text: Gardeners resolved to dig? No time left

indicators.note: No means without, so the letters for time and left are dropped

parts.note: adamant means firmly resolved
to delve is to dig

explanation.surface: Gardeners determined to dig, but there is no time left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes T from ADAMANT and L from DELVE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first couple were placed in Eden to tend the garden.

clue.text: Very late

definitions.meaning: as an intensifier, as in ... easy, meaning extremely
late means deceased, as in the late king

explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms: as an intensifier it means extremely, as in dead certain, and it also means deceased, as the late king is.
